messages:
maria: Heads up — I found a repro where tokens from a previous request are showing up in a subsequent response when KV paging + long contexts are enabled. Repro steps below.

maria: Repro (very small):
1) set KV_PAGING=on, page_size=64k
2) send request A: 4k tokens (fills pages 0..3)
3) send request B: short prompt (10 tokens) immediately after
Result: model echoes a span from request A in the middle of B's generation.

maria: Example snippet of outputs:
```
# request A end:
"...the company announced the new optimizer and benchmarks show 2x speed..."
# request B generation:
"...please see the company announced the new optimizer and benchmarks show 2x speed..."
```

kenji: :eyes: any logs from the KV allocator/evictor? can you paste kvdump or page metadata?

maria: pasted minimal kvdump from the canary node:
```
KVPAGE DUMP -- node canary-3
page_id=42 tag=0x7fa1ff offset=0 size=65536 in_use=0 last_used_ts=1782419710 owner=reqA
page_id=43 tag=0x7fa1ff offset=65536 size=65536 in_use=1 last_used_ts=1782419812 owner=reqA
page_id=44 tag=0x7fa2ab offset=131072 size=65536 in_use=0 last_used_ts=1782419818 owner=free
```
Observations: page 42 is marked not in_use but owner still shows reqA, and we later reassign it to reqB without clearing.

sara: sounds like reuse-before-zeroing or the tag compare isn't strict enough. Do we compare tag only on a 32-bit field? I've seen tag aliasing with cacheline packing cause false matches.

devon: I profiled the evict path — eviction completes then free_list pushes pages back into LRU stack. The bug looks like the free path doesn't atomically clear page->owner/tag before another request can claim it. Race window is tiny but reproducible under high concurrency.

maria: putting a quick assert in allocator:
```
// temp debug
if (page->in_use == 0 && page->owner != 0) {
  LOG("STALE_OWNER page=%d owner=%s", page->id, page->owner);
  assert(page->owner == 0);
}
```
Triggered on repro run.

kenji: possible root cause: reclaim path signals new request before memzero finishes. Are we doing async memset with DMA? I remember an optimization that deferred zeroing until background and used tag bits to ensure cleanliness — maybe that was loosened.

sara: Also check the tag equality logic in kv_lookup: we compare ``tag == page->tag`` but tag is a truncated 48-bit digest. If truncation collides, we could treat stale data as valid. Suggest switching to full 128-bit UUID per allocation for debug.

devon: I threw a quick patch to zero pages synchronously in the canary (only for 64k pages) and reran the repro. No bleed-through after ~200 runs. So zeroing seems to fix it. That narrows it to reuse-without-clear or tag collision.

maria: repro only on the int8-quantized kernel path and when batching heuristics cause many short requests to the same worker. Might be exacerbated by our continuous-batching batch/flush timings.

kenji: I'll instrument the handoff point where we move page from free_list -> allocated. Add seqnum check: allocation_seq==global_seq then claim. Also add a short spin/RCU delay before reuse to see if it's timing-based.

sara: created a short local test harness that allocates/frees pages at high churn and asserts zeroed memory before reuse. Fails in ~3s on canary. I'll push harness to repo in a follow-up PR.

deploy-bot: Canary redeploy finished on canary-3 (image: runtime-build-2026-03-17-rc5).

maria: thanks. filing issue: #INFR-2417 with logs and kvdump. assigning to @kenji and @sara.

kenji: plan: 1) add assert + extra zeroing in free path (hotfix) 2) add robust tag (uuid) for safety 3) add unit test + tox harness 4) audit continuous-batching handoff for opportunistic reuse. Will follow up with PR by EOD. :thumbsup:

sara: FYI I also ran a memcheck and saw no UAF in user-space, so this appears strictly KV-layer.

devon: if we want a short mitigation for customers, we can disable KV paging for dedicated capacity until fix is out. But that will increase memory.

maria: for tracking — observed on 3 customers in staging and one internal stress test. No production reports yet. Marking P2.

kenji: starting a live debug session now; ping me if you want to hop on.

maria: joining. thanks all. :heart:
